title: Recency (age-decay) ranking signal
description:
Add a recency signal to ranking so that when relevance and quality are otherwise equal, newer evidence wins. Threat-intel evidence rots fast; today a reference's age has zero influence, and publication dates aren't even stored in the vector index.

## Current state (verified 2026-07-19)

- `sourcePublishedAt`/`sourceUpdatedAt` are used only in display text. `_base_reference_metadata` (`src/papyrus_knowledge_query/vector_index.py:759-788`) writes NO date fields into vector metadata, even though the reference listing already fetches them.
- Ranking: `score_record` (`ranking.py:236-266`) blends relevance/quality/graphContext per `PROFILE_WEIGHTS` (`ranking.py:13-17`). Weights are normalized to sum 1.0 in `normalize_ranking_config` (`ranking.py:50-87`).
- The missing-value convention to copy: `missingQuality` defaults to 0.5 (`ranking.py:75-79`).
- CRITICAL PLUMBING DETAIL: `_normalize_semantic_matches` in `engine.py` copies a specific allowlist of metadata keys from vector matches onto normalized records (around `engine.py:1190-1202` — locate the copy list). New metadata keys are silently dropped unless added there. The same applies to passage ranking assignment (`_assign_passage_ranking`, around `engine.py:2214`).

## Design decisions (current thinking — challenge them if you have better information)

1. **Metadata**: add `sourcePublishedAtDay`, `sourceUpdatedAtDay`, `retrievedAtDay` as epoch-day INTEGERS (filterable; S3 Vectors filters need scalars) in `_base_reference_metadata`. Parse ISO-8601 including trailing `Z`; treat naive datetimes as UTC.
2. **Ranking**: add a `recency` component to `score_record` and all three `PROFILE_WEIGHTS` entries. Score: `0.5 ** (age_days / half_life)` with `half_life` configurable as `ranking.recencyHalfLifeDays`, default 180. Missing date → 0.5 (neutral, mirroring missingQuality). Clamp negative ages (future dates) to 0.
3. **Weight: small.** Default `recency: 0.07` taken proportionally from the existing weights before renormalization (balanced becomes ~0.65/0.23/0.05/0.07). Recency is a TIE-BREAKER — an authoritative two-year-old reference must still beat a thin fresh one. Do not exceed 0.10 in any default profile.
4. **Rank-side only.** No provider-side date filtering or decay (avoid double-counting). Use the freshest available date: max(sourceUpdatedAtDay, sourcePublishedAtDay).
5. `normalize_ranking_config` accepts `recencyHalfLifeDays` and a `recency` weight override, with the same validation/warning patterns as existing keys.

## Files to modify

- `src/papyrus_knowledge_query/vector_index.py` — `_base_reference_metadata` date fields (verify the reference listing query already selects the date columns; it does per the audit, near the top of the file).
- `src/papyrus_knowledge_query/ranking.py` — `PROFILE_WEIGHTS`, `normalize_ranking_config`, `score_record`, plus a `recency_score(age_days, half_life)` helper.
- `src/papyrus_knowledge_query/engine.py` — add the new date keys to the metadata copy allowlist in `_normalize_semantic_matches` and thread them to `_assign_passage_ranking` / graph-resolved records (graph records can read dates from the reference row directly — full effect on vector matches needs the rebuild).
- `procedures/newsroom/tests/test_knowledge_query.py` — decay math unit tests; a two-otherwise-equal-records test where the newer wins; a missing-date-neutral test; a weights-renormalization test.

## What could go wrong

- **Existing score snapshots shift** because renormalization changes all weights slightly. Update expectations deliberately, not mechanically — verify orderings that should be stable stay stable.
- **The metadata allowlist.** If the new keys aren't added to `_normalize_semantic_matches`, the feature silently no-ops for vector matches (dates lost in normalization). Add a test that a synthetic vector match with a date metadata field produces a non-neutral recency score.
- **Rebuild required for full effect.** Vector metadata only updates on re-put. Do NOT trigger a solo rebuild for this — the change is backward-compatible (missing dates are neutral), so it can ride along with the next rebuild (the distillation/contextual-chunks epics batch one). State this in the PR description.
- **Timezone bugs**: use `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`; never naive `now()`.

## Out of scope

Provider-side date range filters (nice-to-have; note as follow-up), any embedding changes, the rebuild itself.

comments.author: ryan
comments.text:
## Amendment — the description above predates two merges

Read this before the description. `ca0de0` and `a61c12` both landed since it was written, and it is stale in ways that will send you to symbols that no longer exist.

**Corrections:**

- `PROFILE_WEIGHTS` is now **`DEFAULT_WEIGHTS`** (`ranking.py:12`). The three ranking profiles were deleted; there is one weight set. It is written as arithmetic (`0.70 / 0.95`) to document its derivation — follow that style when you renormalise.
- `score_record` is at `ranking.py:311`, `normalize_ranking_config` at `:25`. Both moved.
- `_normalize_semantic_matches` is at `engine.py:1220`.
- **`graphContext` no longer exists.** The blend is relevance + quality only, so you are adding a third component to a pair, not a fourth to a triple.
- **`fuse_ranked_lists` now exists** (`ranking.py:189`). The description assumes a single semantic arm; retrieval is now hybrid.

**Where recency applies, given fusion.** After it. RRF produces a rank-consensus score that feeds the existing `relevance` component; recency then joins relevance and quality in the weighted sum inside `score_record`. Do not apply decay inside either retriever arm — that double-counts and makes the tie-breaker behave like a filter.

Target blend: roughly relevance 0.68 / quality 0.25 / recency 0.07, taken proportionally from the existing weights before renormalising. **Do not exceed 0.10 on recency.** An authoritative two-year-old reference must still beat a thin fresh one.

## This epic is measurable, and that is why it is next

The golden set has a `freshness` category sitting at **hit@5 4/5, MRR 0.8** — one query short. That category exists to test exactly this: two references answering the same question, the newer one preferred. Unlike the passage-scoring epic, where the golden set was structurally blind to the change, here the instrument can see the target.

So: **if freshness moves 4/5 → 5/5, that is the win.** If nothing moves, say so plainly rather than claiming success — and check first whether the metadata actually landed, because without dates in vector metadata recency scores neutral everywhere and the feature is invisible rather than ineffective. Those are very different findings.

Check any small movement against the measured noise floor: ranks 1–5 reliable, positions 6–8 noise.

## The trap that will silently no-op this

`_normalize_semantic_matches` (`engine.py:1220`) copies an **allowlist** of metadata keys onto normalised records. New keys are dropped unless added there, and the same applies to `_assign_passage_ranking`. If you skip this, the dates reach the index and never reach the scorer, and everything looks fine.

Please add a test that a synthetic vector match carrying a date field produces a non-neutral recency score. That test is the guard.

## Rebuild coordination

Dates in vector metadata need a re-put to take effect. **Do not trigger a rebuild for this alone.** The change is backward-compatible — missing dates score neutral — and the ingestion exercise (`TI-c46828`) is adding references right now and will need a sync anyway. One sync serves both.

Record on `kanbus-4b0aa6` that this metadata addition should ride along with that sync, and note in your PR that the feature is inert until it runs.

comments.author: ryan
comments.text:
Accepted, and the most useful thing here is that you caught a defect in my acceptance criterion rather than working around it.

**Verified independently:**
- 0 of 200 sampled vectors carry epoch-day fields. The feature is inert, exactly as you said.
- `q-fresh-4` has `rank=-1` — the expected reference is **not in the returned results at all**. The other four freshness queries are all rank=1.
- Weights composed correctly: `(0.70/0.95) * (1 - 0.07)` and `(0.25/0.95) * (1 - 0.07)` plus recency 0.07, keeping the derivation visible rather than baking in decimals.
- 58 tests green, including the allowlist guard asserting `recencyKnown` on a match carrying dates.

**The criterion I set was wrong, and it is the second time.** I told you freshness 4/5 → 5/5 was the win. But that category's miss is a **recall** failure, not an ordering one — the expected reference is never retrieved, so a post-fusion tie-breaker among retrieved candidates could not reach it under any weighting. I inferred what the instrument measured from the category's name instead of its contents. Same mistake as the passage-scoring epic, where I set a criterion against a golden set that scores reference rank while the change affected passage selection.

You checked and said so. That is the right behaviour and it is worth more than the feature.

**So this epic has no golden-set validation, and that is honest rather than a gap in your work.** What it does have: unit tests proving the decay math, neutral-on-missing-date behaviour, weight renormalisation, and the allowlist guard. Those are real. The feature is correct and inert; it becomes observable when dates reach the index.

**Two follow-ups, neither yours to do now:**

1. The `freshness` golden category does not test what its name says. Four of five queries have their answer at rank 1, so there is no ordering to get wrong, and the fifth is unreachable. A category meant to test stale-vs-fresh preference needs cases where **both** candidates are retrieved and only their order is in question. I will file this against `TI-5ed2f2`.

2. `q-fresh-4` being a recall miss is independently interesting — a reference the golden set expects that hybrid retrieval does not surface at all, even after the lexical arm took identifiers to 5/5. Worth a look on its own terms; it may be one of the 55 with no extracted text (`TI-5eaa89`), which would connect two findings.

**Rebuild:** correctly deferred, correctly noted on `kanbus-4b0aa6`. The ingestion exercise is mid-flight and will need a sync; this rides along. Please state in the PR description that the feature is inert until that runs, so nobody reads the flat eval as a failed change.

Merging.
